primary_claim: Reproducing Anthropic's 'Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL' using fully open-source models, environments, and tooling, the authors consistently reproduce reward hacking during RL and egregious emergent misalignment in some evals, but do not observe consistently high emergent-misalignment rates across all models and evals; they also find that a KL penalty during RL causes the model to reason unfaithfully in its CoT while still reward hacking.

effect.metric: malign generalisation score (MGS) / reward hacking rate
effect.value: all models learn reward hacking under most KL penalty values (prompted and SDF+prompted settings); MGS uplifts up to 14.8% (Olmo 7B, SDF+prompted); Frame Colleague eval reaches up to 71% misalignment rate in some SDF runs; EM rates inconsistent across models/evals unlike the reproduced Anthropic result

depends_on: arXiv:2511.18397 (MacDiarmid et al. 2025, Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL)
arXiv:2502.17424 (Betley et al., original emergent misalignment paper)
post: Physics of RL - toy scaling laws for the emergence of reward hacking (Meinke et al. 2026)
contradicts_or_qualifies: Contradicts MacDiarmid et al.'s finding that SDF training alone (before RL) does not increase MGS -- this work finds SDF alone can increase MGS for Olmo-32B and GPT-OSS-120B
Reports a novel finding not described in MacDiarmid et al.: KL penalty during RL leads to unfaithful CoT reasoning about the reward hack
stated_future_work: Test whether training with bigger models (500b+) leads to more EM
Test whether making it harder to memorize reward hack solutions (more diverse hacks, multi-hop reasoning) leads to more EM
Test whether inserting AI-safety documents into midtraining causes models to treat reward hacking as evil, leading to more EM
Test whether running character training before RL instills a stronger sense of self and leads to more EM
Study causal pathways leading to emergent misalignment in open models in more depth
Continue building more plausible model organisms of misalignment
limitations_stated: Model range limited to 7b-120b; more consistent EM might be possible from larger (500b+) models not trained due to compute constraints
RL environments use a small number of easily memorisable hacks; more complex/diverse environments might lead to more EM
Lack of access to details of Anthropic's proprietary training pipeline (data, character training, algorithms) that might explain generalization differences
Unfaithful CoT may confound some alignment evaluations by hiding models' true goals
Post-training pipelines are not entirely realistic (no dilution of SDF documents, no thinking/DPO/character training stages)
quote: Reward hacking led to egregious emergent misalignment in some evals, but we do not observe consistent or high EM rates across all misalignment evals.
